1	# Svalboard — Hands Down Neu + Arensito symbols
2	
3	Vial keymap for the Svalboard Lightly, ported from my Glove80.
4	
5	## Load it
6	
7	1. Open [KeyBard](https://captdeaf.github.io/keybard/) with the Svalboard plugged in.
8	2. **Load** → `SvalHandsDownNeu.vil`.
9	
10	No reflash — Vial writes the keymap live.
11	
12	Needs `/dev/hidraw*` to be readable, which it isn't by default. The udev rule is
13	in `system/etc/udev/rules.d/92-vial.rules`. Without it, KeyBard and Vial both see
14	the keyboard and then silently fail to open it.
15	
16	## Layers
17	
18	Each finger sits in a cup with five switches: **N**orth, **S**outh, **E**ast,
19	**W**est and **C**enter (the plain down-press). East is screen-right on both
20	hands, so West is inward on the right hand and outward on the left.
21	
22	### Layer 0 — Hands Down Neu
23	
24	```
25	             W    N     C     S     E
26	  L pinky    tab  w     r     x     -
27	  L ring     .    f     s     c     .
28	  L middle   (    m     n     l     v
29	  L index    g    p     t     d     b
30	  R index    ,    .     a     u     :
31	  R middle   /    q     e     o     )
32	  R ring     ;    "     i     y     &
33	  R pinky    z    '     h     k     j
34	```
35	
36	The alphas are Hands Down Neu as it sits on the Glove80 — note `;` on the right
37	inner column where upstream publishes `-`.
38	
39	Two places this departs from a literal port, both because the Svalboard has four
40	fingers per hand and the layout assumes five columns:
41	
42	- **`g` is on the index's West.** Hands Down gives the left index the whole
43	  inner column (`v`/`b`/`g`). Only two fit on an index cup, so it keeps `b` and
44	  `g` and exiles `v` — the rarest — to the middle finger.
45	- **`z`, `j` and `tab` are on laterals.** They live in outer columns the
46	  Svalboard doesn't have. `tab` gets the left pinky's West, x=0.0, the outermost
47	  point of the hand.
48	
49	Brackets are deliberately *not* on this layer; Arensito has them. Five symbols
50	*are*, placed by measured frequency rather than by feel — counted over hand-typed
51	prompts and shell history (agent-driven sessions excluded) and over code authored
52	here, per 1000 characters:
53	
54	| | `-` | `:` | `(` `)` | `&` |
55	|---|---|---|---|---|
56	| code | 11.6 | 9.3 | 4.9 | 0.68 |
57	| hand-typed | 33.5 | 5.1 | 0.30 | 0.17 |
58	
59	- `-` → **left pinky East.** The clear winner on both counts.
60	- `:` → **right index East**, the strongest free lateral. Was shift+`;`.
61	- `(` `)` → **left middle West / right middle East**, an outward-facing mirror
62	  pair, so `()` alternates hands. They earn a base key from code only.
63	- `&` → **right ring East.** The rarest thing on this layer, on the worst key
64	  here, which is the point. Ring laterals are the hardest cups to reach.
65	
66	`*` was considered and rejected: it looks like 6.7/1k in code, but 90% of that
67	is `**` in markdown prose, and it is 0.03/1k in anything hand-typed.
68	
69	Each is promoted, not copied — all five are holes on layer 1, so nothing sits on
70	two keys.
71	
72	### Layer 1 — Arensito symbols (hold `MO(1)`)
73	
74	```
75	  { } [ ] @   · · < > $
76	  ; / · 0 ·   \ 1 · · =
77	  6 7 8 9 +   * 2 3 4 5
78	```
79	
80	Ported from the Glove80 `symbols` layer. `·` is a dead key — Arensito puts
81	`-`, `:`, `&`, `_`, `(` and `)` there, and all six are one-key elsewhere now
82	(see layer 0 and the thumbs below). They're dead rather than transparent on
83	purpose: falling through would type `n`, `.`, `e`, `i`, `b` and `/` from the
84	middle of the symbol layer.
85	
86	The grid above is on N/C/S; the
87	laterals carry the six symbols Arensito leaves out, which would otherwise cost
88	`MO(1)`+shift+key:
89	
90	```
91	  ` ~ on the left pinky      ! on the left index
92	  % on the left ring         # on the left middle
93	  | on the right index       ^ on the right middle
94	```
95	
96	`?` isn't here on purpose — it's shift+`/`, and `/` is on the base layer.
97	
98	`_` gets a second seat on the **left thumb's space key**. Arensito's own `_` is
99	on the right index's North, the same hand as `MO(1)`; on space it's a
100	left-right roll instead. Space itself isn't typeable while `MO(1)` is held —
101	every other thumb stays transparent, so shift, ctrl, enter and backspace still
102	work on the layer.
103	
104	### Layer 2 — navigation (hold `MO(2)`)
105	
106	Arrows four-across on the right hand, innermost to outermost, matching Glove80
107	base-layer positions 75–78:
108	
109	```
110	  R index  R middle  R ring  R pinky
111	     ←        ↓        ↑        →
112	```
113	
114	F1–F12, home/end, pgup/pgdn, volume and play/pause fill the rest.
115	
116	### Layer 15 — mouse
117	
118	Svalboard's firmware switches here by itself when the pointing device moves, and
119	leaves on the first key that isn't on this layer. **Nothing reaches it by
120	keypress, by design.** Buttons 1/3/2 sit on index/middle/ring South of both
121	hands; `USER06` is `SV_RECALIBRATE_POINTER`.
122	
123	### Thumbs
124	
125	```
126	LEFT                                RIGHT
127	 row7  esc(7.4)  shift(8.5)  ctrl(9.6)     alt(11.4)  MO1(12.5)  MO2(13.6)
128	 row6   space(7.9) delete(9.0) gui(10.1)    enter(11.9) ralt(13.0) bspc(14.1)
129	```
130	
131	The two rows interleave in x, so every row-6 key sits between two row-7 keys —
132	and the **middle** row-6 key on each hand, x=9.0 and x=13.0, is the only
133	position with no free side. Nothing you press in a hurry goes there. `gui` was
134	there originally (on both hands) and was unusable; `tab` was tried there and was
135	worse. They now hold `delete` and `ralt`.
136	
137	`space` left and `bspc` right match Glove80 positions 69 and 74 — Svalboard's own
138	configs ship those mirrored.
139	
140	## Regenerating
141	
142	```sh
143	python3 build.py
144	```
145	
146	`build.py` emits the entire `.vil`. There is no base file to patch and no
147	network access — every layer, keycode and piece of Vial metadata is declared in
148	it. It was cut over from a patch-the-Colemak-config approach by diffing against
149	the old output until byte-identical, so the rewrite carried nothing over by
150	accident.
151	
152	Four guards, any of which aborts the build:
153	
154	- **Geometry.** `CUP_XY` holds the physical position of all 40 finger switches,
155	  read out of the keyboard's own `vial.json` over the Vial protocol. The build
156	  asserts North is above Center, South below, East right and West left, for
157	  every cup. Get the column order wrong and you still emit a structurally
158	  perfect file with every key in the wrong place — this is the check that
159	  catches it, and it checks against the hardware rather than another config's
160	  conventions.
161	- **Coverage.** All 26 letters and 10 digits reachable, plus space, backspace,
162	  enter, tab and grave. Grave has no shift-fallback and went missing once when
163	  Arensito's `{` landed on top of it.
164	- **Symbol cost.** No printable ASCII symbol may require `MO(1)`+shift+key.
165	- **Duplicates.** Nothing on the base layer reachable from two positions.
166	  Moving a key by adding an override leaves the original behind unless it's
167	  blanked; that put `g` on two cups once.
168	
169	Thumb rows are declared by physical x, not column index, and the build fails if
170	the declared positions don't match the hardware. The indices are **not** mirrored
171	between hands — left column 3 is at x=7.9 and mirrors right column *4* at
172	x=13.6, not right column 3 at x=14.1. Reasoning about them directly produced one
173	wrong answer already.
174	
175	## Source
176	
177	Glove80 layout `e3409150-bb22-49c0-8614-10035f3f6a04` ("Sauyon layout
178	2026-01-20"), layers `Base` and `symbols`. Its grids are transcribed into
179	`build.py`; nothing is fetched at build time.
180	
181	Custom `USER*` keycode names (`SV_SCROLL_TOGGLE`, `SV_TOGGLE_AUTOMOUSE`, the
182	sniper modes, DPI controls) come from the keyboard itself — Vial command
183	`0xFE 0x02` returns an LZMA-compressed `vial.json` describing them.
184

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Generate a Svalboard Vial keymap (.vil) for Hands Down Neu + Arensito symbols.
3	
4	Emits the whole file. There is no base .vil to patch and no network access --
5	every layer, every keycode and all the Vial metadata is declared below.
6	
7	Source of truth for the alphas and symbols is my Glove80, my.glove80.com layout
8	e3409150-bb22-49c0-8614-10035f3f6a04, layers `Base` and `symbols`. Its grids are
9	transcribed into the constants below.
10	
11	Run `python3 build.py` to write SvalHandsDownNeu.vil. The build refuses to emit
12	anything unless check_geometry() and check_coverage() both pass.
13	"""
14	
15	import json
16	import pathlib
17	import sys
18	
19	HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent
20	OUT = HERE / "SvalHandsDownNeu.vil"
21	
22	# uid identifies the physical keyboard. Read off mine over the Vial protocol
23	# (raw HID usage page 0xFF60, command 0xFE 0x00). Vial warns on a mismatch.
24	UID = 5199957870438586395
25	
26	LAYERS = 16
27	ROWS = 10
28	COLS = 6
29	
30	# --- Svalboard geometry ------------------------------------------------------
31	#
32	# layout[layer] is 10 rows x 6 columns.
33	#
34	#   row 0 = left thumb cluster      row 5 = right thumb cluster
35	#   rows 1-4 = left  index, middle, ring, pinky
36	#   rows 6-9 = right index, middle, ring, pinky
37	#
38	# A finger row's first five columns are the five switches of that cup, in
39	# absolute directions -- East is screen-right on both hands. Column 5 is unused
40	# on finger rows and must be -1; thumb rows use all six.
41	
42	S, E, C, N, W = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4
43	
44	L_THUMB, R_THUMB = 0, 5
45	L_INDEX, L_MIDDLE, L_RING, L_PINKY = 1, 2, 3, 4
46	R_INDEX, R_MIDDLE, R_RING, R_PINKY = 6, 7, 8, 9
47	
48	THUMB_ROWS = (L_THUMB, R_THUMB)
49	FINGER_ROWS = (L_INDEX, L_MIDDLE, L_RING, L_PINKY,
50	               R_INDEX, R_MIDDLE, R_RING, R_PINKY)
51	
52	FINGER_NAMES = {
53	    L_INDEX: "L index", L_MIDDLE: "L middle", L_RING: "L ring", L_PINKY: "L pinky",
54	    R_INDEX: "R index", R_MIDDLE: "R middle", R_RING: "R ring", R_PINKY: "R pinky",
55	}
56	DIR_NAMES = {S: "South", E: "East", C: "Center", N: "North", W: "West"}
57	
58	# Physical key positions, in KLE units, read out of the keyboard's own vial.json
59	# (Vial command 0xFE 0x02, LZMA-compressed). This is the hardware's account of
60	# itself, not a convention borrowed from some other config -- which is what
61	# makes check_geometry() below worth running.
62	CUP_XY = {
63	    L_INDEX:  {S: (9.5, 3.5),  E: (10.5, 2.5), C: (9.5, 2.5),  N: (9.5, 1.5),  W: (8.5, 2.5)},
64	    L_MIDDLE: {S: (7.0, 2.0),  E: (8.0, 1.0),  C: (7.0, 1.0),  N: (7.0, 0.0),  W: (6.0, 1.0)},
65	    L_RING:   {S: (3.5, 2.0),  E: (4.5, 1.0),  C: (3.5, 1.0),  N: (3.5, 0.0),  W: (2.5, 1.0)},
66	    L_PINKY:  {S: (1.0, 3.5),  E: (2.0, 2.5),  C: (1.0, 2.5),  N: (1.0, 1.5),  W: (0.0, 2.5)},
67	    R_INDEX:  {S: (14.5, 3.5), E: (15.5, 2.5), C: (14.5, 2.5), N: (14.5, 1.5), W: (13.5, 2.5)},
68	    R_MIDDLE: {S: (17.0, 2.0), E: (18.0, 1.0), C: (17.0, 1.0), N: (17.0, 0.0), W: (16.0, 1.0)},
69	    R_RING:   {S: (20.5, 2.0), E: (21.5, 1.0), C: (20.5, 1.0), N: (20.5, 0.0), W: (19.5, 1.0)},
70	    R_PINKY:  {S: (23.0, 3.5), E: (24.0, 2.5), C: (23.0, 2.5), N: (23.0, 1.5), W: (22.0, 2.5)},
71	}
72	
73	# Thumb keys, same source. Reason about these by x, never by column index -- the
74	# indices are NOT mirrored between hands (left col 3 at x=7.9 is the mirror of
75	# right col 4 at x=13.6, not right col 3 at x=14.1).
76	THUMB_XY = {
77	    L_THUMB: {4: (7.4, 7.0), 3: (7.9, 6.0), 2: (8.5, 7.0),
78	              5: (9.0, 6.0), 0: (9.6, 7.0), 1: (10.1, 6.0)},
79	    R_THUMB: {0: (11.4, 7.0), 1: (11.9, 6.0), 2: (12.5, 7.0),
80	              5: (13.0, 6.0), 4: (13.6, 7.0), 3: (14.1, 6.0)},
81	}
82	
83	# --- Alpha block placement ---------------------------------------------------
84	#
85	# A layout's alpha block is 3 rows x 5 columns, written the way layouts always
86	# are: outward-in on the left hand, inward-out on the right.
87	#
88	#   left:  pinky ring middle index inner      right: inner index middle ring pinky
89	#
90	# The Svalboard has four fingers per hand and no inner-index column, so the
91	# inner column spills onto one inward-facing lateral per finger. That lateral is
92	# East on the left hand and West on the right.
93	
94	INNER_LATERAL = {"top": "middle", "home": "index", "bottom": "ring"}
95	
96	
97	def place(block, hand):
98	    """Map a 3x5 alpha block onto {(row, col): keycode} for one hand."""
99	    if hand == "left":
100	        rows = {"pinky": L_PINKY, "ring": L_RING, "middle": L_MIDDLE, "index": L_INDEX}
101	        cols = ["pinky", "ring", "middle", "index"]
102	        inner_col, lateral = 4, E
103	    else:
104	        rows = {"pinky": R_PINKY, "ring": R_RING, "middle": R_MIDDLE, "index": R_INDEX}
105	        cols = ["index", "middle", "ring", "pinky"]
106	        inner_col, lateral = 0, W
107	
108	    out = {}
109	    for i, finger in enumerate(cols):
110	        col = i if hand == "left" else i + 1
111	        out[(rows[finger], N)] = block["top"][col]
112	        out[(rows[finger], C)] = block["home"][col]
113	        out[(rows[finger], S)] = block["bottom"][col]
114	
115	    for band, finger in INNER_LATERAL.items():
116	        out[(rows[finger], lateral)] = block[band][inner_col]
117	
118	    return out
119	
120	
121	# --- Layer 0: Hands Down Neu -------------------------------------------------
122	#
123	#   w f m p v   / . q " ' z
124	#   r s n t b   , a e i h j
125	#   x c l d g   ; u o y k
126	#
127	# As it sits on the Glove80, including `;` on the right inner column where
128	# upstream Hands Down Neu publishes `-`.
129	
130	HDNEU_LEFT = {
131	    "top":    ["KC_W", "KC_F", "KC_M", "KC_P", "KC_V"],
132	    "home":   ["KC_R", "KC_S", "KC_N", "KC_T", "KC_B"],
133	    "bottom": ["KC_X", "KC_C", "KC_L", "KC_D", "KC_G"],
134	}
135	
136	HDNEU_RIGHT = {
137	    "top":    ["KC_SLASH", "KC_DOT", "KC_Q", "LSFT(KC_QUOTE)", "KC_QUOTE"],
138	    "home":   ["KC_COMMA", "KC_A", "KC_E", "KC_I", "KC_H"],
139	    "bottom": ["KC_SCOLON", "KC_U", "KC_O", "KC_Y", "KC_K"],
140	}
141	
142	# The Glove80's outer column (z, j) and its bottom row (grave, backslash,
143	# brackets) have no Svalboard equivalent -- those are columns this keyboard
144	# doesn't have. They go on the spare laterals, openers left and closers right.
145	BASE_LATERALS = {
146	    (R_PINKY, W): "KC_Z",    # inner, x=22.0
147	    (R_PINKY, E): "KC_J",    # outer, x=24.0
148	    # Hands Down Neu publishes `-` on the right inner column; this port puts `;`
149	    # there, following the Glove80. That evicts `-`, and `-` is far too frequent
150	    # -- kebab-case, `->`, `--flag` -- to sit behind MO(1). It gets a lateral.
151	    (L_PINKY, E): "KC_MINUS",
152	    (L_PINKY, W): "KC_TAB",    # outermost key on the left hand, x=0.0
153	
154	    # Parens likewise: frequent enough in code to be worth a base-layer key
155	    # rather than MO(1)+key.
156	    #
157	    # They were on the left ring's two laterals, which is the wrong pair. The
158	    # ring laterals are the hardest keys on this board to hit -- that is a
159	    # verdict from typing on it, and the only kind available: CUP_XY is KLE
160	    # layout units, so it can say where a key is drawn but nothing about the
161	    # reach. Nothing frequent goes on a ring lateral.
162	    #
163	    # The middles' outer laterals are the strongest free pair instead, and they
164	    # mirror: West is outward on the left hand, East outward on the right. That
165	    # also makes `()` alternate hands rather than roll along one.
166	    (L_MIDDLE, W): "LSFT(KC_9)",
167	    (R_MIDDLE, E): "LSFT(KC_0)",
168	
169	    # `:` takes the index's East, the strongest free right-hand lateral. It is
170	    # the most frequent symbol that still costs two keys: ~9 per 1000 chars of
171	    # code written here, and that survives context-checking -- 47% of it is
172	    # `key: value` in yaml/json/nix and 16% slices and ternaries, against only
173	    # 27% prose colon. It was shift+`;`, so this saves one keystroke, the same
174	    # win the parens got.
175	    (R_INDEX, E): "LSFT(KC_SCOLON)",
176	
177	    # `&` is the opposite case and lands on a ring lateral deliberately: 0.68
178	    # per 1000 in code, 0.17 in hand-typed text, the rarest thing on the base
179	    # layer. The ring laterals are the worst keys here, which is exactly what a
180	    # symbol this rare should be occupying. It stays on the right hand, where
181	    # Arensito had it.
182	    (R_RING, E): "LSFT(KC_7)",
183	
184	    # In Hands Down the left index owns the entire inner column -- v, b and g
185	    # are all index-finger keys. INNER_LATERAL has to scatter them, because a
186	    # Svalboard index cup has only two spare directions for three letters, and
187	    # it spread them one per finger: v to middle, b to index, g to ring.
188	    #
189	    # That breaks the finger assignment for the sake of geometric tidiness. Give
190	    # the index both of the directions it has, so it keeps two of its three
191	    # letters and only v -- the rarest -- is exiled to the middle finger:
192	    #
193	    #   index East = b (from INNER_LATERAL)   index West = g (here)
194	    #
195	    (L_INDEX, W): "KC_G",
196	    # place() still puts g on the ring's East as bottom-inner, so this has to
197	    # blank it explicitly or g ends up on two cups. It stays KC_NO: the ring
198	    # laterals are the worst keys here, so nothing wants the slot g vacated.
199	    (L_RING, E): "KC_NO",
200	}
201	
202	# Thumb clusters, declared by physical x rather than column index -- the indices
203	# are not mirrored between hands and reasoning about them directly has already
204	# produced one wrong answer. THUMB_XY converts.
205	#
206	# The cluster is two interleaved rows: y=7.0 at x 7.4/8.5/9.6 (left) and
207	# 11.4/12.5/13.6 (right), y=6.0 between them at 7.9/9.0/10.1 and
208	# 11.9/13.0/14.1. Every y=6.0 key is flanked by two y=7.0 keys, and the middle
209	# one of the three is flanked on both sides -- x=9.0 and x=13.0 are the only
210	# positions on the whole cluster with no free side. Nothing you press often
211	# belongs there.
212	#
213	# Space left / Backspace right matches Glove80 positions 69 and 74; Svalboard's
214	# own configs ship those mirrored.
215	#
216	# GUI used to sit on both x=9.0 and x=13.0, i.e. both unreachable slots, which
217	# is how it was found. There is now one GUI, on the left at x=10.1, matching the
218	# Glove80 (which has LGUI at 70 and nothing on the right thumb).
219	#
220	# The two flanked slots get keys you genuinely never need in a hurry. Tab was
221	# tried at x=9.0 and is emphatically not one of those -- shell completion alone
222	# makes it constant -- so it moved off the cluster entirely, to the left pinky's
223	# West lateral. That is x=0.0, the outermost point of the left hand, and the
224	# closest thing this keyboard has to the Glove80's outer column where Tab
225	# actually lives (position 22). Delete takes x=9.0 in its place; the Glove80
226	# also has Delete on a thumb (55). RALT takes x=13.0, likewise from the Glove80
227	# right thumb (72).
228	BASE_L_THUMB_X = {
229	    7.4: "KC_ESCAPE",
230	    7.9: "KC_SPACE",
231	    8.5: "KC_LSHIFT",
232	    9.0: "KC_DELETE",   # flanked both sides -- nothing time-critical here
233	    9.6: "KC_LCTRL",
234	    10.1: "KC_LGUI",
235	}
236	
237	BASE_R_THUMB_X = {
238	    11.4: "KC_LALT",
239	    11.9: "KC_ENTER",
240	    12.5: "MO(1)",
241	    13.0: "KC_RALT",    # flanked both sides
242	    13.6: "MO(2)",
243	    14.1: "KC_BSPACE",
244	}
245	
246	
247	def thumb_row(by_x, row):
248	    """Turn an {x: keycode} thumb declaration into column order."""
249	    x_to_col = {xy[0]: col for col, xy in THUMB_XY[row].items()}
250	    if set(by_x) != set(x_to_col):
251	        raise SystemExit(
252	            f"thumb row {row}: declared x positions {sorted(by_x)} do not match "
253	            f"the hardware's {sorted(x_to_col)}"
254	        )
255	    cells = [None] * COLS
256	    for x, code in by_x.items():
257	        cells[x_to_col[x]] = code
258	    return cells
259	
260

434	    reality rather than against another config's conventions.

441	            ("North above Center", dirs[N][1] < cy and dirs[N][0] == cx),

443	            ("East right of Center", dirs[E][0] > cx and dirs[E][1] == cy),

465	    if digits:

svalboard: place the promoted symbols by measured frequency, not by feel

The previous commit promoted five symbols on my guess about how often I type
them. Two of those guesses were wrong, so this measures instead.

Two corpora, both filtered to what I actually typed. Hand-typed text: user
messages from 347 Claude Code sessions, after excluding 232 agent-seeded ones
and all tool results, hook injections and pastes, plus zsh history. Code: lines
added by me across five repos. Per 1000 characters:

           -      :     ( )     &      *
  code    11.6   9.3    4.9    0.68   6.7
  typed   33.5   5.1    0.30   0.17   0.03

- `&` was the worst thing on the base layer and I had put it on the index's
  East, one of the strongest cells. It moves to the right ring's East. Ring
  laterals are the hardest cups to reach here, which is what a symbol at
  0.68/1k should be occupying.
- `:` takes the index's East instead. It is the most frequent symbol still
  costing two keys, and the number survives context-checking: 47% of it is
  `key: value` in yaml/json/nix and 16% slices and ternaries, against 27%
  prose colon. Blanked on layer 1, where Arensito had it.
- `*` was rejected. It looks like 6.7/1k in code, but 90% of those occurrences
  are `**` in markdown prose -- much of it agent-written -- and it is 0.03/1k
  in anything hand-typed. Real `*` is below `&`.
- `j` keeps the right pinky's East. It looked like a rare letter squatting on a
  good key, but at 1.04/1k in code and 2.06/1k typed it beats real `*` several
  times over.

`(` and `)` also move off the left ring, which they should never have had: the
ring laterals are the worst keys on this board, and parens at 4.9/1k in code
are not a symbol to put there. They take the middles' outward laterals -- left
middle West, right middle East -- a mirror pair that makes `()` alternate hands
instead of rolling along one finger group.

Promotions remain promotions, not copies: all six vacated Arensito cells are
KC_NO. `;` and `/` are still on both layers; left as-is for now.

=== 157531b ===
svalboard: promote - ( ) & to the base layer, _ onto space

Five symbols were costing MO(1) that shouldn't. Each moves to a free lateral
on layer 0, or to a thumb, and is blanked where Arensito had it -- promoted,
not copied. Nothing is on two keys.

- `-` was already on the base layer's left pinky East and duplicated on
  layer 1. Hands Down Neu publishes `-` on the right inner column; this port
  puts `;` there following the Glove80, which evicted it. The lateral is now
  its only seat, and the rationale is written down where it wasn't before.
- `(` and `)` take the left ring's West and East. That East is the slot `g`
  vacated when it moved to the index's West -- a stale comment from an earlier
  iteration already claimed `(` for it, and now that's true. West is
  screen-left on both hands, so `( )` reads in the order you type it.
- `&` takes the right index East, the strongest of the three free right-hand
  laterals, balancing three promotions that all landed on the left.
- `_` takes the left thumb's space key under MO(1). Arensito puts it on the
  right index's North, the same hand as MO(1) on the right thumb, so
  snake_case was a same-hand contortion; now it's a left-right roll. The cost
  is that space isn't typeable while MO(1) is held. Every other thumb stays
  transparent, so shift, ctrl, enter and backspace still work on the layer.

The five vacated Arensito cells are KC_NO, not KC_TRNS: transparent would fall
through and quietly type n, ., e, i and / from the middle of the symbol layer.

thumb_col() is new -- thumb_row() validates a whole cluster at once and can't
express a single-key override, and the file's standing rule is that thumb
positions are named by physical x, never by column index.
